subject: Hosting & Audit readiness: BAA / SOC2 evidence and path recommendation
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johansson <emma@medsymphony.com>
Cc: MedSymphony Security <security@medsymphony.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T15:02:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + recommended hosting path (HIPAA / audit focus)

Emma — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and our recommended next steps based on the audit needs you described (BAA required; auditor will want SOC 2 Type II artifacts + evidence around data retention and key management):

Summary of options we discussed (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to launch, but not appropriate if you need customer-managed networking or strict on-prem controls for PHI. Can operate under a BAA; SOC2 artifacts are available, but network isolation is limited.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): Provides tenant isolation and predictable performance; generally the best fit for organizations that want a managed environment with stronger isolation while keeping Redwood-managed infra. Supported under BAA and we can provide SOC2 evidence and per-customer audit logs.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full isolation with customer-managed network and optional air-gapped deployments — the path if your compliance team requires control over key management or on-prem auditability. Longer lead time and enterprise contract required.

Our recommended path given MedSymphony's needs (BAA + auditor evidence requests):
1) Start with Dedicated capacity for a production pilot (gives isolation and fast time-to-value).
2) Parallel legal & security work: exchange a draft BAA and assemble an SOC2 evidence package (we can produce a SOC2 artifact bundle: control descriptions, SOC2 summary, sample audit logs, retention configs).
3) If your security team or auditor requires customer KMS/HSM or on-prem archive, we prepare a Private deployment plan for Q4 cutover.

Action items / asks from your side:
- Confirm whether the auditor requires customer-managed KMS/HSM or if a provider-managed KMS (with key separation options) is acceptable.
- Share the vendor questionnaire you mentioned (we can pre-fill).
- Preferred date window for a 30-minute legal/security sync next week.

Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level SOC2 artifacts we can provide), baa-template-v2.docx (sample BAA). Also linking a HubSpot deal and our shared drive with compliance docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example

If you want, we can also include a short pricing sketch for Dedicated vs Private during the next call.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Yes, we will need a signed BAA before sending live PHI. Our auditor prefers the vendor to support customer-managed KMS for key separation, but we sometimes accept provider KMS if the vendor can demonstrate strict key isolation and export controls. Can you confirm Redwood's capabilities here?
- SOC2 Type II is required; auditor will ask for evidence of access logging, retention settings, and personnel access controls for the period covered by the report.
- Attached is our vendor questionnaire (medsymphony-vendor-questionnaire.xlsx) — we started filling a few sections. Can you have your security or compliance engineer complete sections on logging, encryption, and data residency?

We are aiming to finalize vendor selection in the next 4–6 weeks, so timelines are a bit compressed.

Two asks: can we get a 30-min evidence review slot with your security contact (no deep technical level needed, more for the auditor to validate artifacts) and a draft BAA redline from your legal team?

Appreciate it — Emma

- Private (VPC/on-prem): 8–12+ weeks, depending on KMS/HSM integration and customer network readiness.
